claim.why_it_matters: The last two rows of the 13.14.1 meta-language term table fell out of the table into a loose paragraph, so a table parser loses where validate-status-clause and value-clause (data-item or table format) are defined.

verdict.reasoning: On the printed page (PDF p274, printed 252) the Term/Subclause table under 'where the following meta-language terms are described' lists nine rows in one uniform column layout, running from class-clause to value-clause, with validate-status-clause (13.16.60) and value-clause (13.16.61) as its last two rows. In page-274.md the pipe table stops at '| usage-clause | 13.16.58, USAGE clause |', and those two rows appear after a blank line as a plain paragraph joined by a backslash line break. The words and clause numbers match the PDF exactly, so no text is lost. What is lost is table membership, which is a real structural defect: anything that reads the table gets 7 rows where the page has 9. The claim quotes both sources accurately, and 'structural' is the right severity because the defect is not normative.
